metadata.summary: Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their game against Chelsea on Saturday.
metadata.content: Man Utd boss Michael Carrick to remain in charge vs Chelsea and given chance to turn situation around | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man Utd boss Michael Carrick to remain in charge vs Chelsea and given chance to turn situation around Man Utd's under-pressure head coach Michael Carrick being given the opportunity to turn current situation around with the 13-time Premier League winners currently on an eight-game winless run in all competitions and one point above the relegation zone Danyal Khan Sky Sports News Reporter @DanyalHKhan Tuesday 27 October 2026 14:26, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Danyal Khan is at Manchester United's Carrington training ground with the significant news that Michael Carrick will remain in charge heading into the weekend Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their game against Chelsea on Saturday. The under-pressure United head coach was thought to be on the brink after Sunday's crushing 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth, but he and the players are being given the chance to turn the current situation around. United's director of football, Jason Wilcox, and chief executive, Omar Berrada, were at Carrington discussing Carrick's future on Monday. It is understood they had already been considering alternatives for the head coach role. However, Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision has been taken to give him at least one more match. messages.text: Smith ruled out of Cape Town Test late due to neck injury

metadata.summary: Steve Smith has been ruled out of Australia's third Test decider against South Africa in Cape Town after it was confirmed late on Tuesday morning that the batter had not fully recovered from a neck injury.
metadata.content: Australia vs South Africa: Steve Smith ruled out of Cape Town Test due to neck injury | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Australia vs South Africa: Steve Smith ruled out of Cape Town Test due to neck injury Steve Smith was a late injury omission for Australia ahead of the series-deciding third Test against South Africa on Tuesday; the 37-year-old had been set to play at Cape Town for the first time since the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal; watch the third Test live on Sky Sports Tuesday 27 October 2026 09:20, UK Image: Steve Smith has been ruled out of Australia's third Test against South Africa Steve Smith has been ruled out of Australia's third Test decider against South Africa in Cape Town after it was confirmed late on Tuesday morning that the batter had not fully recovered from a neck injury. Australia gave the 37-year-old a chance to prove his fitness ahead of the Test match, which would have seen Smith return to Cape Town for the first time since the infamous 'Sandpapergate' scandal at Newlands in 2018. Smith appeared to injure himself during his first spell at the crease during Australia's second Test defeat to South Africa in Gqeberha, in which the hosts levelled the series 1-1. messages.text: 'Beyond my wildest dreams' - Kane first English winner of Ballon d'Or in 25 years

metadata.summary: Harry Kane has become the first English winner of the Ballon d'Or in 25 years after being honoured at a ceremony in London.
metadata.content: Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or: Bayern Munich striker becomes first English winner of award in 25 years | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or: Bayern Munich striker becomes first English winner of award in 25 years Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or at London ceremony; Bayern Munich striker becomes first English winner of award in 25 years; England captain hit 73 goals for club and country last season; ex-Tottenham forward beat Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal to prize Tuesday 27 October 2026 10:11, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Kane wins the 2026 Ballon d'Or as the Bayern Munich striker becomes the first English winner of the award in 25 years Harry Kane has become the first English winner of the Ballon d'Or in 25 years after being honoured at a ceremony in London. Michael Owen was the last player from England to receive the prestigious individual accolade in 2001, but Kane's incredible 73-goal haul last season for club and country earned him the award from French magazine France Football. Bayern Munich forward Kane was a popular winner in the capital and has followed in the footsteps of Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Owen as a Ballon d'Or winner from England.
